[BURHAN:v3p356/r1] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | Plural forms conventionally associated with a small count can denote abundance; the Qur'an supplies many examples, including الصابرين والصادقين and المؤمنين والمؤمنات.
[BURHAN:v4p426/r1] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | The phrase بعضهم من بعض expresses a shared relation: believers are allies, while the comparison with 3:34 evokes common lineage; the cited disbelievers instead disavow one another. | mentions 2:166
[BIQAI-FULL:v3p356/r11] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The believers’ mutual alliance and their commands to good, rejection of wrong, prayer, almsgiving, and obedience stand as the faithful pattern beside the warning about earlier disbelieving peoples.
[BIQAI-FULL:v3p356/r12] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The faithful are promised God’s mercy, while His might and wisdom ground the promise.
[BIQAI-FULL:v3p357/r10] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Their alliance means they stand together against outsiders like one body, whose other members respond with fever and wakefulness when one organ suffers.
[BIQAI-FULL:v3p357/r11] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Maʿrūf is everything recognized and permitted by the revealed law.
[BIQAI-FULL:v3p357/r12] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | They likewise forbid wrong, showing no favoritism to anyone.
[BIQAI-FULL:v3p357/r13] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | They perform prayer with all its pillars, conditions, and limits, mindful of their Lord and drawing aid from it for whatever befalls them.
[BIQAI-FULL:v3p357/r14] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Zakat is support for their poor, joining service to fellow creatures to service of the Creator; it contrasts with the hypocrites' withholding hands (9:67). | mentions 9:67
[BIQAI-FULL:v3p357/r15] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Their obedience to God and His Messenger signals their good conduct and gracious companionship.
[BIQAI-FULL:v3p357/r16] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The promised mercy parallels the hypocrites' being forgotten after forgetting God (9:67). | mentions 9:67
[BIQAI-FULL:v3p357/r17] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The road is rough and difficult, so the traveler depends on God's mercy, which is gracious treatment after forgiveness; no one can cross or arrive without it.
[BIQAI-FULL:v3p357/r18] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | God's invincible power lets Him aid His party and grant mercy without anyone preventing it; His wisdom makes His decree impossible to undo.
[BIQAI-FULL:v3p357/r19] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Believers remain victorious over every corrupter while they preserve mutual loyalty and its accompanying virtues.
[BIQAI-FULL:v3p357/r8] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | After describing the hypocrites' mutual allegiance and threatening those like them with destruction for persisting without reflection, he turns to believers to invite repentance through hope in their state.
[BIQAI-FULL:v3p357/r9] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Unlike the hypocrites' 'some of them are of others,' the believers are allies without imitation or caprice: each follows the Messenger by conclusive proof, according to individual understanding, showing sound and rooted faith.

[DURR-FULL:v4p233/r6] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās says their alliance is brotherhood in God: they love one another for God's sake, and their loyalty is for God.
[DURR-FULL:v4p233/r7] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | Salman transmits the Prophet's saying that people known for good in this world are people of good in the next, and people of evil here are people of evil there; a parallel mursal version is from Abū ʿUthmān.
[DURR-FULL:v4p233/r8] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | Abū Mūsā transmits a Prophetic report portraying good and evil as two beings raised on Judgment Day: good gives its people glad tidings, while evil drives its companions to cling to it.
[DURR-FULL:v4p233/r9] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · سعيد بن المسيب | reports | Saʿīd b. al-Musayyib attributes to the Prophet the saying that after faith, the chief of reason is treating people considerately, and that no one is ruined after consultation; he repeats the saying about good and evil people in both lives.
[ITQAN:v2p474#2/r5] ITQAN, d. 911 · author | holds | In a promise or threat, سـ reinforces certainty even if fulfillment is delayed; in 9:71 it assures that God will show mercy, as it can reinforce a threat of revenge.
[ITQAN:v3p275/r2] ITQAN, d. 911 · author | holds | These parallel endings show that mercy or a plea for forgiveness can fittingly end with “Mighty, Wise,” since God’s mercy and pardon are sovereign and wise.
[ITQAN:v3p307/r6] ITQAN, d. 911 · author | holds | Hypocrites share doubt and hypocrisy but lack common open allegiance; believers and declared unbelievers aid one another, unlike the hypocrites whose hearts are divided. | mentions 9:71, 8:73, 59:14
[BURSEVI:v3p351#2/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Establishing prayer means constant remembrance and vigilant, present hearts that trade cannot distract; these are people of unveiling and hearts, opposite to those who forgot God. | mentions 9:67
[BURSEVI:v3p351#2/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Unlike hypocrites who withhold their hands, they pay obligatory zakat and give any surplus beyond necessary sufficiency, purifying themselves of worldly attachment. | mentions 9:67
[BURSEVI:v3p351#2/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | They obey every command and prohibition, in contrast to hypocrites described by complete rebellion and departure from obedience. | mentions 9:67

[BURSEVI:v3p351#3/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | God will pour out mercy through support and victory, save them from Hell’s punishment and the pain of distance from Him, and admit them to Paradi

[BURSEVI:v3p351#3/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | God’s might explains His promise: He can honor His allies, subdue His enemies, and bestow favor on those who obey Him.
[BURSEVI:v3p351/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | A Persian couplet contrasts worldly sovereignty with the greater security of a poor person’s kingdom; the wise should reflect on worldly and afterlife conditions until death and burial.
[BURSEVI:v3p351/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Believers share the true religion and monotheism, help each other in religious and worldly matters, and guide one another to higher degrees through spiritual training and purification.
[BURSEVI:v3p351/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | They enjoin every good, including faith and obedience, and encourage one another to seek God, the real good, as expressed in the saying I loved to be known.
[BURSEVI:v3p351/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | They forbid every evil, including disbelief and sins that sever a person from God in this world and beyond.
[ALUSI-FULL:v10p135/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The passage describes believers' good state now and in the hereafter after describing their opponents' state in this life and the next.
[ALUSI-FULL:v10p135/r10] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · صاحب التقريب | reports | The author of al-Taqrib argues that the future particle emphasizes whatever follows because affirmation with sa- contrasts with negation by lan, whether the result is promise, threat, or something else.
[ALUSI-FULL:v10p135/r11] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · ابن حجر | rejects | Ibn Hajar rejects the claim that sa- itself guarantees the promised outcome: certainty comes from context, and he says the claim serves al-Zamakhshari's mistaken doctrine that reward is necessary.
[ALUSI-FULL:v10p135/r12] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · ابن قاسم | rejects | Ibn Qasim counters Ibn Hajar's criticism: a transmitted point cannot be dismissed by that argument, and accusing the imams of inattention arises from a desire to object.
[ALUSI-FULL:v10p135/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Their mutual guardianship contrasts with the earlier description of hypocrites as one another's kind; the wording changes to convey mutual support and solidarity. | mentions 9:67

[ALUSI-FULL:v10p135/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Paying zakat reverses the hypocrites' grasping their hands shut. | mentions 9:67

[ALUSI-FULL:v10p135/r8] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The demonstrative refers to the believers and women believers characterized by the preceding excellent qualities; its distant form carries the emphasis discussed earlier.
[ALUSI-FULL:v10p135/r9] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari and others say the future particle strengthens the promise of mercy.
[ALUSI-FULL:v10p136/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | God is mighty, able to do anything and never prevented from willing it, and wise, placing things where they belong, including reward and punishment; this grounds the promised mercy.
[ELMALILI:9:71-72/r1] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Elmalılı renders the mutual awliyāʾ relation as male and female believers being one another's walīs or protectors.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p262/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | This clause answers 9:67 and identifies the people who receive pardon as those attached to the believers; its sentence continues the linked sequence of clauses. | mentions 9:67
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p262/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Believers share the bond of Islamic allegiance as equals; its sense conveys sincerity and mutual support, unlike hypocrites who seem to arise from one another in vices. | mentions 9:67
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p262/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The added description of believers as establishing prayer honors prayer as the greatest form of enjoining what is right.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p263/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Giving alms by believers contrasts with the hypocrites' withholding their hands. | mentions 9:67

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p263/r4] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The future particle reinforces the certainty of coming mercy; with a present verb it conveys what قد conveys with a past verb, as in 93:5. | mentions 93:5
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p263/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The demonstrative signals that the people described are worthy of what follows because of the qualities listed before it.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v10p263/r6] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | God's might enables Him to benefit His allies, and His wisdom places reward with those who deserve it; this explains His mercy.
[TABATABAI:11:36-49#26/r4] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | All strength and honor belong to God, so Islam permits reverence for others only when it leads back to God, as in honoring the Messenger, believers, and divine signs.
[TABATABAI:9:64-74#6/r1] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Believers, despite differences of number and gender, form one unified community; therefore they mutually assume responsibility for and manage one another's affairs.
[TABATABAI:9:64-74#6/r2] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Because this mutual guardianship extends throughout the community, believers enjoin right and forbid wrong among one another as well.
[TABATABAI:9:64-74#6/r3] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Prayer and zakat are the two firm pillars of the law: prayer links God and creation through worship, while zakat links people through social dealings.

[TABATABAI:9:64-74#6/r5] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | In another respect, obeying God's revealed laws is included in obeying the Messenger, who proclaims truth and calls people to the fundamentals and branches of religion.

[TABATABAI:9:64-74#6/r7] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | God's might cannot obstruct his mercy, and his wisdom entails no defect, weakness, or arbitrary judgment; these attributes explain the promised mercy.
